title: A Confession for the Alibi
premise: Retired detective Coral Amberdale has built a quiet life around his failing bookshop, secretly solving the 'accidental' deaths the police ignored—until a murdered woman is found wearing clothes stolen from his own closet, a message meant for him alone. The victim is tied to the one case he never solved: the disappearance of his partner, officially closed when a man confessed and then died awaiting trial. As the trial of an innocent scapegoat approaches, Coral must unravel who orchestrated both the old frame-up and this new killing, discovering that the corruption reaches into the very department that once protected him. In the end, Coral sacrifices his anonymity—and nearly his life—to expose the truth, finding that the ragtag family of misfits gathered around his bookshop is worth more than the invisibility he treasured.
about_author: Casper Montrose is the pen name of a former small-town court reporter who spent fifteen years watching justice bend without breaking. He writes mysteries from a coastal cottage, assisted by an opinionated cat named Verdict.

chapters.title: The Weight of Quiet Things
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. We meet the failing bookshop, its found-family regulars, and Coral's private habit of solving unsolved deaths from his back room. A cold, contented rhythm established—then shattered by a knock at the door.

chapters.title: Dressed in Someone Else's Clothes
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Police summon him: a woman found dead in the harbor warehouse, wearing his distinctive cardigan and scarf. The staging is personal, intimate—a message only he could read. Fear creeps in beneath his detective's calm.

chapters.title: Three Accidents Too Many
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, with flashback texture. Detective Ilsa Vann, the young officer who suspects Coral's secret successes, presses him for help while quietly building a file on him. Uneasy alliance forms; trust is rationed.

chapters.title: The Case That Swallowed Its Own Tail
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. He revisits the closed file on his partner Marlowe's disappearance—the confession, the dead confessor, the trial that never happened. Old grief resurfaces as he realizes the new victim worked at the courthouse.

chapters.title: A Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She investigates the victim independently and finds payments funneled through a shell company connected to retired Captain Braddock—Coral's old mentor. Her loyalty to procedure wars with her instinct about Coral.

chapters.title: What the Bookshop Keeps
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. His irregulars—teen runaway Dex, insomniac widow Pru, ex-con barista Milo—notice his distraction and begin protecting him in clumsy, touching ways. Found-family warmth deepens even as danger closes in.

chapters.title: The Confessor's Widow
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. He tracks down the widow of the man who confessed to Marlowe's murder; she reveals her husband confessed under pressure and left a hidden letter naming someone above him. Hope rekindles—then her house burns that night.

chapters.title: Ashes and Alibis
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The arson looks like another accident, but Ilsa finds Coral's fingerprints on the investigation trail and must decide whether he's a suspect or a target. Tension between them sharpens into wary partnership.

chapters.title: Twenty-Two Years of Tuesdays
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Reconstructing his last case with Marlowe, he realizes they were investigating Braddock's evidence-theft ring when Marlowe vanished. The confession was manufactured; the alibi was bought. Rage replaces grief.

chapters.title: The Scapegoat's Daughter
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. He visits the imprisoned man's daughter, who begs him to clear her father's name before the posthumous conviction is sealed. Coral promises what he may not be able to deliver—an emotional turning point.

chapters.title: Someone Is Reading My Mail
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Evidence surfaces that the killer has been inside the bookshop; a rare book contains microfilm of the original case files. Paranoia blooms—who among his circle could be compromised? Trust frays.

chapters.title: Pru Knows Everyone
chapters.summary: Pru's POV. The widow's insomnia-fueled gossip network yields a name: a courthouse clerk who handled both cases and recently came into money. But before she can tell Coral, she's attacked outside the shop.

chapters.title: Blood on the First Editions
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Pru survives, barely. Coral realizes the killer is eliminating every thread he pulls, and that the bookshop itself was chosen as ground zero. He sends his found family away; they refuse to go.

chapters.title: Braddock's Long Goodbye
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Confronting his dying former mentor, Coral receives a half-confession: Braddock covered for someone higher, someone still serving. The captain dies mid-sentence, leaving a chess piece clutched in his hand.

chapters.title: The Move That Ends Games
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Decoding the chess piece—a queen—Ilsa matches it to Deputy Chief Halloway, now overseeing the trial. But her evidence chain is thin, and reporting it would end her career. She chooses the truth anyway.

chapters.title: An Invitation in Chalk
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A chalk outline drawn on the bookshop floor, sized for Coral, with a note: 'Trial starts Monday.' The killer wants him as the final witness—or the final exhibit. Terror and resolve fuse.

chapters.title: Every Alibi Has a Seam
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Working through the night with Dex's computer skills and Milo's street contacts, the team finds the seam: Halloway's alibi for Marlowe's night rests on a logbook entry only the clerk could forge.

chapters.title: The Clerk Who Counted Wrong
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. They find the clerk alive but terrified, hiding in a motel. Her testimony ties Halloway to the forged confession, the payments, and the new murders—but she'll only speak if Coral surrenders himself first.

chapters.title: Trading Myself for the Truth
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral agrees to meet Halloway alone, wearing a wire, betting his life that vanity will make the deputy chief confess. The handoff goes wrong; Coral flees into the harbor district, hunted.

chapters.title: Where Marlowe Sleeps
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, climax. Cornered in the warehouse where it all began, Coral confronts Halloway and learns Marlowe's true fate. Outnumbered, he's saved by his found family and Ilsa arriving together—the invisible man, seen at last.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Isla's POV, courtroom coda. The wire recording and clerk's testimony break the case open; the scapegoat's name is cleared posthumously. Coral watches from the gallery, no longer hiding, as the machinery of power grinds against its own.

chapters.title: Open Sign
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Weeks later, the bookshop reopens with a new shelf: books about wrongful convictions, proceeds to the exonerees' fund. Coral finally hangs Marlowe's photo by the register. The quiet he wanted has become a quiet he chose.
